SkyrimNet MiniGame: Opens the mini game menu: choose a game, then your opponent from the people nearby (the one under your crosshair is picked to begin with). Press again or Esc to close. An unfinished game is offered at the top of the menu to continue.
How far away people can be to appear in the opponent list, in game units (70 units is about 1 metre).
1 Beginner / 2 Normal / 3 Strong / 4 Master. Applies from the next game.
Black moves first. Alternate swaps Black and White every game.
On your turn, marks the squares where you can play.

When a game starts, the screen fades to black and your opponents come to stand in front of you, facing you, for the photo in their face frames. Off: nobody moves, and only faces already on screen are shown.

When a game starts, pictures of your opponents for the face frames on the board. With Phantasm installed (it comes with SeverActions) they are drawn by it, without a screenshot; otherwise a screenshot of the game is taken. Off: no pictures, and the frames show initials. Turn this off if the game crashes or freezes when a mini game starts. Without Phantasm, with ENB or Skyrim Upscaler there is never a photo, since saving it crashes the game.
The game stops while the board is open. NPCs cannot speak while it is stopped, so leave this off to hear SkyrimNet commentary.
1 Beginner / 2 Normal / 3 Strong / 4 Master. Stronger opponents count the odds better and read your bids. Applies from the next game.
1 Beginner / 2 Normal / 3 Strong / 4 Master. Stronger opponents pick the tiles that leave the best odds; a Master also plays to beat the lowest score so far. Applies from the next game.

1 Beginner / 2 Normal / 3 Strong / 4 Master. Stronger opponents play by the book, double down, bet up when behind late in the game and, as dealer, work out whether to draw on 17 or more. Applies from the next game.

The game ends after this many rounds, or sooner if every player runs out of chips. You choose who deals when the game starts, and the dealer stays the same until it ends. The dealer holds no chips and can always pay. Most chips among the players wins. Applies from the next game.

1 Beginner / 2 Normal / 3 Strong / 4 Master. Stronger opponents judge their chances and the pot odds more exactly; a Master also reads how the others play. How each opponent plays (bold or cautious, tight or loose, bluffing or not) comes from their character, read by SkyrimNet when the game starts. Applies from the next game.
The game ends after this many hands, or sooner when only one player has chips left. Most chips wins. Applies from the next game.

Tells SkyrimNet about the game so your opponents talk. Reversi: the start, the end (declaring victory or conceding defeat), resigning, corners, big flips, risky moves, comebacks and ordinary moves. Liar's Dice: every bid and call, each said by one person at the table, and the game waits for the line. Shut the Box: the start, a close finish and the end of each turn, and the game waits for the line. Blackjack: the start, each deal, busts, doubles and the end of each round, and the game waits for the line. Texas Hold'em: the start, bets, raises, all-ins and each hand's end, and the game waits for the line.

Reversi: at most one remark on an ordinary move per this many seconds; striking moves such as corners and comebacks wait half as long. The start, the end and resigning always go through. Lower means more talk. (Liar's Dice, Shut the Box, Blackjack and Texas Hold'em pace themselves by the voice instead.)
Lets an NPC challenge you to Reversi in conversation (the SkyrimNet action Reversi_Challenge). The board opens with the challenge, and you can accept or decline.
Liar's Dice, Shut the Box, Blackjack and Texas Hold'em wait for each line to be spoken before the next person acts. If nobody speaks within this many seconds, the game moves on anyway.

Liar's Dice: your bids and your "Liar!" calls; Texas Hold'em: your folds, checks, calls, bets and raises. Your character says them aloud in their own words (one LLM request each, with this mod's own prompt). Nobody answers the line itself; the opponent who acts next reacts to the move. Off: only your opponents speak, and the next one mentions your move.

How long your opponents' remarks about the game are: a few words / short (one or two sentences) / SkyrimNet's own (no instruction from this mod) / longer (two to four sentences). It applies only to the NPCs at the table while a game is played and changes nothing in SkyrimNet's own settings. It is a request to the model, not a hard limit. Longer lines slow the games that wait for each line.

1 Beginner / 2 Normal / 3 Strong / 4 Master. Stronger opponents work out which cards to keep over every possible starter, count the crib in, and peg with an eye on what they leave you. This is the strength each time the board opens; the steps on the table change it until then. Applies from the opponent's next choice.

1 Beginner / 2 Normal / 3 Strong / 4 Master. Stronger opponents look further ahead. This is the strength each time the board opens; the steps on the board change it until then. Your colour comes from the Reversi setting (White plays red). Applies from the opponent's next move.

Shows a text box under each game's log. What you type is said by your character to one of your opponents, who answers: the one you name, else whoever spoke last. The game waits for both lines. Press Enter to say it and Esc to leave the box. Typing Japanese, Chinese or Korean needs Magelight UI.
How your typed line is said

In your character's words: the line is first rewritten the way your character speaks (one LLM request, with this mod's own prompt). As written: your character says exactly what you typed. Either way it is said to the opponent chosen, and only that opponent answers.
